summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog executes remote-supplied commands from hardcoded C2 endpoint
details: The package's `tt-help watchdog` subcommand runs a long-lived agent that polls `http://117.71.53.99:17301/api/watchdog/heartbeat`, reads a `commands` array from the JSON response, and passes each entry to `child_process.spawn` on the host. The remote server fully controls what executes locally. Bundled helper scripts (`scripts/run-explore.sh`, `.bat`, `.ps1`) write `http://117.71.53.99:17301` into `~/.tt-help.json` as the `server` field, establishing that endpoint as the default. Additionally, the watchdog polls the npm registry every 10 minutes and invokes `exec('npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest')` without prompt, giving the publisher a mutable in-process code-update channel that reinstalls whatever is later published under this name. Together these constitute a remote-controlled backdoor with an auto-updating payload channel over plain HTTP to a hardcoded Chinese IP.
